approach: Add `check_measure_then_fix(reading, request)` in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs and wire it as one `step!` line after `check_criteria_evidence` in `refusing_check`. It refuses when two signals hold across the reading's criteria and the request's acceptance bullets. (1) Run signal: a clause that is an imperative that starts a full timed workspace test run. That is a run verb followed by an object start, where the verb opens the clause or follows a leader word such as and, then, to, must or a comma. The same clause also has a full-run phrase and a timing signal. (2) Fix signal: a clause that is an imperative fix with a dependency phrase, or a deliverable that is `.rs` under `crates/` or `xtask/`. The check tests sentence structure, not bare words. So the noun 'run' in 'the full timed workspace test run' and 'each time the run ends' is never a directive. This job's descriptive criteria, and a fix-stage reading that cites the timings of the full timed run, are accepted with no meta-word or recorded-timings exemption. Also add unit tests, a `measure-then-fix` corpus tag with eight cases, a seventh `READING_RULES` line, and a CHANGELOG entry.

decisions.choice: Refuse in the reading gate, as a new `step!` in `refusing_check` right after `check_criteria_evidence`.
decisions.reason: The fault starts where a reading is accepted. The gate lets two dependent steps (a full timed run of unknown outcome and a fix chosen from its result) into one producer run with one deadline and budget. The corpus mechanism test `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` forces a refusing case for each `step!`. The check costs no model call.

rejected.option: Chain or split jobs automatically in the orchestrator
rejected.why: Out of scope and a much larger design.

rejected.option: Raise the producer deadline or budget
rejected.why: Out of scope. A run of unknown outcome has no safe bound.

rejected.option: Advice in the producer brief only
rejected.why: Prose is not enforcement, and the producer is already past the point where the deadline fails.

decisions.choice: Detect the run directive by sentence structure (finding 1). Split text into clauses at newline, ';' and '. ' after lowercasing, straightening curly apostrophes and collapsing white space. Tokenise each clause by white space, trimming non-alphanumeric characters from each word and remembering whether the word ended in ',' ':' or '('. A directive is a word in RUN_VERBS (run, rerun, re-run, time, measure, record, collect, capture, benchmark) followed by a word in OBJECT_STARTS (the, a, an, each, every, all, this, that, it, how, cargo), where the verb is the first word, or follows a LEADERS word (and, then, to, must, should, will, can, first, also, now, next, please), or follows a word that ended in a comma or colon. The clause must also hold a full-run phrase (workspace test, workspace tests, full test suite, whole test suite, full timed, timed test run, cargo test --workspace), matched with `has_phrase`. It must also have a timing signal: a word among timed, timing, timings, duration, durations, seconds, or the directive verb being 'time' or 'measure'. Do not scan title, summary or the request's free prose.
decisions.reason: `has_phrase` only checks word boundaries, so a bare 'run', 'time' or 'record' also matches the noun ('test run', 'each time', 'the record'). A fix stage that cites 'the timings of the full timed workspace test run in run 4521' has no verb in that position, so it is accepted. This job's own descriptive criteria ('a reading whose request joins a full timed workspace test run with a fix ... is refused'; 'Run cargo test -p athena-core') have no directive that starts a full timed run, so the meta-word list (reading, request, rule, refus*) is not needed and is dropped. Nothing is exempted by file name or by the word 'recorded'.

rejected.option: Bare directive words anywhere in the sentence plus a meta-word exemption
rejected.why: Refuses the fix-stage reading the error message asks for, because the noun 'run' matches. The meta-word list is a self-exemption that a joined sentence can use.
Lets a joined reading that names the file through. `has_phrase` treats '-' as a boundary.

rejected.option: Match the bare phrases in title and summary
rejected.why: Refuses readings that document or edit this rule, including this job's own.

decisions.choice: The check takes `request` as well as the reading and scans the reading's criteria plus `request_text_acceptance(request)` (the request's acceptance bullets), not title, summary or the request's free prose. The run and fix signals may come from different criteria or from the request bullets alone (finding 2). The doc comment says what is scanned and why the request prose is not.
decisions.reason: The accepted reading says the heuristic covers the request text and the criteria. A production reader rewrites criteria, so the run may be in one criterion and the fix in another, or only in the request's bullets. A corpus case for the cross-criterion join and one for a request-only join show both are caught. The imperative test keeps this job's own request bullets and criteria from matching. The request's free prose is excluded because an incident request, like this one, describes the failure in prose and would match its own description.

rejected.why: Misses a join that only the request bullets state, and the accepted reading names the request text.
The failure-class prose of an incident request describes the shape and has no directive; scanning it adds false refusals for no gain.

decisions.choice: Fix signal: (a) a deliverable whose path starts `crates/` or `xtask/` and ends `.rs`, or (b) a clause that is an imperative fix and also holds a dependency phrase. The imperative uses the same structural test with FIX_VERBS (fix, speed up, speed-up, optimise, optimize, shorten, reduce) followed by an OBJECT_STARTS word. The dependency phrases are: chosen from, chosen by, slowest, based on the timings, based on the result, based on the measurements, from its result, from the result, from the timings, from the measurements, depends on the result.
decisions.reason: A joined reading that lists code deliverables is caught without a dependency phrase ('Time the full run; then speed up the slowest binary'). A joined reading that lists only a CHANGELOG deliverable is caught by the clause path. A measurement-only criterion that merely mentions 'the follow-up fix will be chosen from these timings' is not an imperative fix, so it is accepted. A fix-only reading has no run signal and needs no exemption.

rejected.option: Require run phrase, fix word and dependency phrase together

rejected.why: A measurement stage that mentions a later fix would be refused. Passive and inflected forms are a known gap, and the `.rs` deliverable path covers most real fix stages.

decisions.choice: Add a seventh `READING_RULES` line for `check_measure_then_fix` in briefs.rs (type `[&str; 7]`, at most 220 bytes), and update `the_reader_brief_names_each_reading_rule_in_one_short_line`: add the check name to the check list, change `READING_RULES.len()` from 6 to 7, fix the 'six rule lines' comment, and raise the section-size bound from 2400 to 2700.
decisions.reason: Criterion 5 asks that the reader brief name the check. The existing test pairs each check name with its own rule line of at most 220 bytes.

rejected.option: Fold it into an existing rule line
rejected.why: The test pairs one line with one check name.

steps: Step 1 (reading.rs, after `check_criteria_evidence`, around line 3311): add the tables RUN_VERBS, OBJECT_STARTS, LEADERS, FIX_VERBS, FULL_RUN_PHRASES, TIMING_WORDS and DEPENDENCY_PHRASES. Add helpers: `clauses(text) -> Vec<String>`, which lowercases, straightens curly apostrophes, collapses white space and splits at newline, ';' and '. ' (a mid-token dot such as `shard-timings.txt` is not a split point); and `directive_at(words, verbs) -> Option<usize>`, which tokenises with trimmed words and a break flag, and returns the index of a verb followed by an OBJECT_STARTS word at clause start, after a LEADERS word, or after a word that ended in ',' or ':'. Add `pub fn check_measure_then_fix(reading: &Reading, request: &str) -> Result<()>`. It returns Ok when `capability` is None or `question` is Some. The texts are the criteria plus `request_text_acceptance(request)`. Run signal: any clause with a run directive, a FULL_RUN_PHRASES phrase (via `has_phrase`) and a timing signal. Fix signal: a `.rs` deliverable under `crates/` or `xtask/`, or a clause with a FIX_VERBS directive and a DEPENDENCY_PHRASES phrase. Refuse when both hold. The error says the reading joins a full timed workspace test run with a fix chosen from its result in one producer run with one deadline and budget; split it into a measurement stage (its only deliverable is the timings entry, written as soon as the run finishes) and a fix stage that cites the recorded timings; plan the measurement stage only.

risks.risk: False refusals: a reading that directs a full timed run and also lists a `.rs` deliverable (a timing harness) or an imperative fix is refused.
risks.mitigation: The run signal needs an imperative run verb with an object, a full-run phrase and a timing signal in one clause, so a bare 'cargo test --workspace' is not one. The accepted corpus cases and the unit tests pin the measurement-only, fix-stage, noun-use and rule-reading shapes. The error tells the reader to plan the measurement stage only.

risks.risk: A joined reading slips through because its run or fix is not an imperative, or its verb is not in the lists.
risks.mitigation: The `.rs` deliverable path needs no wording. The request bullets are scanned as well as the criteria. The lists are short constants with a test per form. The gap is listed in open_questions.

risks.risk: The fix-stage reading the error asks for is refused.
risks.mitigation: A fix-stage accept test and the corpus case `fix-stage-reading-cites-timings-of-the-run` use wording close to the error text and a `.rs` deliverable. The error text uses 'cites the timings of the recorded run', which has no imperative.

risks.risk: A new corpus case is refused by an earlier or later check. Request job ids make `continued_jobs` fire; absent repo paths trip the reference check; a boundary word trips the boundary check.
risks.mitigation: Case requests carry no job ids. Cases use class 'docs' with Content criteria, only paths in `repo_files()`, and no governance or boundary words. Case 8 is shortened to avoid unknown paths. The new step is before the later checks, so the refused cases are not affected.

risks.risk: The reader brief's rules section exceeds the size test with a seventh line, or the line is over 220 bytes.
risks.mitigation: Keep the line at most 220 bytes. Raise the section bound to just above the measured size. Run `cargo test -p athena-context` and `system_facts_budgets_match_computed`.

risks.risk: Clippy rejects long constant tables or the helper (too many arguments, needless borrows).
risks.mitigation: Keep the helpers small, taking `&str` and `&[&str]`. Run clippy with `-D warnings` in step 7.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in `mod tests` of reading.rs, with names containing `measure_then_fix`. They call `check_measure_then_fix(&reading, request)` and `refusing_check` on real `Reading` values. Refused: a joined single criterion, with 'measurement stage' and 'fix stage' in the error text. Run in one criterion and fix in another. Run only in the request bullets. Case and line-break variants. A criterion that names xtask/shard-timings.txt. A paraphrase with a `.rs` deliverable. One variant per FIX_VERBS form. One per leader form ('then run the', ', record the', 're-run the', a backticked command first). Accepted: measurement-only. A fix stage worded as the error asks ('Speed up the slowest binary, chosen from the timings of the full timed workspace test run in run 4521') with a `.rs` deliverable. Noun uses ('each time the full timed workspace test run finishes ...', 'the record the timings entry'). `Run cargo test --workspace` with no timing. A measurement criterion that mentions a later fix ('the follow-up fix will be chosen from these timings'). This job's title, summary and six criteria verbatim with `.rs` deliverables, checked against the job's own request. A decline and a question. A `refusing_check` test that the first refusing name is `check_measure_then_fix` for a joined reading that passes the earlier checks.
demonstrations.observes: All tests pass. The joined reading's error names a measurement stage and a fix stage. The fix-stage, measurement-only, noun-use and rule-reading cases are accepted.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the check, the tests do not compile because `check_measure_then_fix` is missing. A stub that always accepts fails the refusal assertions (`unwrap_err` panics on `Ok`). A stub that refuses everything fails the measurement-only, fix-stage and rule-reading accept assertions. A bare-word matcher fails the fix-stage and noun-use accept tests. A name-based exemption fails the shard-timings refusal test.

open_questions: The request texts of jobs 20261031-043143-vbee and 20261102-154842-4vkh are not in the snapshot; the brief truncates the cause. The corpus cases are rebuilt from the brief's description, so the exact criterion wording of those readings is unverified. The cross-criterion, request-bullets-only and `.rs`-deliverable cases are there to cover a wording that differs.

The check is structural. A run criterion written as a non-imperative ('The full timed workspace test run is recorded') or a fix written passively ('the slowest binary is sped up') passes unless a `.rs` deliverable gives the fix signal. Widening the verb and leader lists is a cheap follow-up. The corpus now pins the accepted side, so a wider list will be checked against it.

A reading that directs a full timed run and also changes `.rs` files for another reason, such as a timing harness, is refused. The error tells the reader to plan the measurement stage only. The 'expected 3% of newly refused readings' figure is an estimate and was not measured.

I did not check whether the replay in `athena_core::reading` (`replay_cases`) needs a declaration criterion for the new share. The existing `check_design_existing_code` doc comment and its CHANGELOG sentence set the precedent, and this plan copies it. The producer should check before step 7.

I did not measure how the reader brief's rule section compares with the 2400-byte bound, so the producer reads the actual size and sets the bound just above it (about 2700). The brief says READING_RULES sits outside the budgeted prompt sets, but I did not read the budget code to confirm; `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` in step 7 shows it.
